Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this
leaf before reading. What I report about content comes only from headings and a
colophon that are written on the leaf itself (transcribed below).

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
====================================================================
Two faces of one paper leaf are supplied (two overviews: image-001 and image-006).

Face A (image-001; tiles 002 upper left, 003 upper right, 004 lower left, 005 lower right)
- Upright, two columns, cursive hand in dark brown/black ink, no ruling visible, no red.
- A numeral in the upper right corner, read "30" (first digit could be 7 or 3).
- Left column: short lines in the vernacular (Italian), arranged in groups of 2, 3, 4
  and 6 lines separated by blank lines; lines begin with slightly enlarged capitals
  and rhyme at the ends (observation). Then a two-line Latin closing formula
  beginning "Explicit", preceded by a large paraph/bracket. Then a two-line
  vernacular couplet. Then two short Latin recipes each with a heading line
  ("Ad ..."). Lower third of the column is blank.
- A pinkish-red stain lies over lines 11-13 of the left column.
- Right column: a heading line at the very top, then a continuous Latin prose
  block of about 29 lines, a blank line, then a second block of 17 lines opening
  with the recipe sign (crossed R). Lower quarter blank.
- Show-through from the other face is visible but faint.

Face B (image-006; tiles 007 upper left, 008 upper right, 009 lower left, 010 lower right)
- Upright, two columns. Gutter on the right, so this is probably the other side
  of the same leaf (tentative).
- Left column: four short recipes, each with a centred heading and a crossed-R
  opening. The fourth is a vertical list of eight ingredient names joined by a
  drawn bracket to a label at the right repeating the heading.
- Right column: a centred heading, then a list of short two- or three-word Latin
  phrases, one per line, each with a capital. The list begins in one sub-column,
  and a second sub-column of 18 entries stands to its right, divided from the
  first by a drawn vertical line with a hook at the top; the left sub-column
  continues below for about 30 more lines. Order of reading between the two
  sub-columns is not certain (see limitations).
- No interlinear glosses, no marginal commentary, no running title on either face.
  No underlining. Nothing looks like text-with-commentary; it reads as a
  miscellany of short items (tentative interpretation).

Areas selected: I read every written line on both faces. Nothing was left unread,
but several words remain uncertain and are marked.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; word? or (?) = uncertain reading;
[illegible] = could not read; "(et)" renders the tironian 2-shaped sign;
"(contra)" renders the 9-like sign with stroke used before ailments;
"R(ecipe)" renders the crossed R; ʒ / ℈ / ℥ render the apothecary weight signs,
which I could not always tell apart.

6. DELETIONS, ADDITIONS, LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
- No clear deletions by strike-through. Possible correction/overwriting in

  neighbours (image-008 L3 left, L13 right, L14 left, L16 left; image-010 L11,
  L18); I cannot tell from the image whether this is a later filling-in or only
  a fresh pen dip.
- Face A left column: the vernacular verses L1-L3 look like the end of a group
  whose beginning is not on this face; the text evidently continues from a
  preceding page that is not in the packet. The first three lines and L16, L18,
  L19 contain words I could not resolve confidently.
- Face A right column L3, L6, L13, L17, L26-27 contain uncertain words; I have
  not smoothed them into sense.
- Weight signs (dram / scruple / ounce) and the quantity ".5." (possibly a form
  of "semis") are not reliably distinguished in my reading.
- Face B right column: the order in which the two sub-columns should be read is
  not determinable from the image (the right sub-column may be a continuation
  squeezed into free space after the left one filled the page, or may be
  read across). Right-hand ends of image-008 L2 and L10 are cut by the
  gutter/page edge; a wider or flatter image of the gutter side would help.
- The folio numeral on Face A is uncertain (30 / 70).
